source.original_title: 06/10/2026 - David Elder x Ben Byrne KL
source.display_title: 06/10/2026 - David Elder x Ben Byrne KL — Follow Up

setter.name: Kyla
setter.evidence: Rep: 'I know you had a conversation with Kyla. looks like you guys had to cover a lot of stuff. I was taking a look at those notes'; prospect later refers to 'a few different numbers, like Sophia, Kyla'

prospect.name: David Elder
prospect.occupation: Owner of his own design and fabrication company (design/research, carpentry, welding, 3D printing); previously a DJ
prospect.family_status: Long-term relationship ended; bought an apartment alone, currently renting it out and living with his parents
prospect.training_background: Highly athletic upbringing — gymnastics, ballet, figure skating, ice hockey, rock climbing, motocross; bodybuilding-style training in early high school; dancing/club culture through his 20s; stopped structured training around 19; deconditioned after COVID, peak weight 210 lb, historically ~150 lb; restarted deliberately ~Sept 2025
prospect.medical: No chronic conditions, no surgeries, no chronic back or shoulder pain. Reports very tight groin/inner-thigh area, knee cartilage discomfort that makes running difficult (switched to jump rope), and a history of many broken bones with no muscle or joint sequelae. Self-directed 1,200-1,280 kcal/day intake and a history of 7-10 day water fasts.

signals: Gained 60 lb after COVID and describes watching his body atrophy: 'to be alive and witnessing yourself partially decompose'
Explicitly wants a former self back: 'I stopped working out maybe when I was like 19' and wants to get back to how he looked and felt
Carries visible regret and describes body dysmorphia, dissociation and an 'existential identity crisis'
Not an optimizer — he is recovering ground, not going good to great

goals.text: Lose the remaining weight — down from 210 to 181, historically around 150
Build physical and mental strength, agility and mobility without becoming a bodybuilder
Master kettlebell and mace movements and stop feeling awkward with them
Build a routine he can carry for the next 40-50 years, until he is old
Be able to ski, snowboard and dance without being wrecked after two days
Fit back into his old clothes and recognise himself again
Create discipline — know which days are on, which are off, and not skip

pains.text: Gained 60 lb after COVID and felt his body atrophy in a way he described as scary and grotesque
Body dysmorphia that led to social isolation and dissociation from himself
Timid about scaling up load — has done two-hand kettlebell swings for two weeks but has not attempted the overhead press because he is scared to push himself
Piecing a programme together from Trevor's free content — 'trying to follow along with the digital breadcrumb trail, which can be very difficult'
Does not know whether he is doing things the right way — 'there's like a lot of components ... I'm doing the best I can on my own'
Skiing and snowboarding became brutally painful; feels schlumped and uncoordinated when dancing
Dislikes gyms and gym culture and has neither the finances nor the physical space for machine-based training
Business is new and cash-poor — not paying himself, renting out his apartment, living with parents
Prior five-month project of 14-hour days wiped out his training effort entirely

objections.raw_quote: it doesn't seem unreasonable. It just seems like, personally, it's a lot for me. Because I'm just like starting out on my business and it's been tricky getting clients and having like consistent work where I can take on that much money.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection ('is it literally just the amount'), confirmed belief in the programme, then asked to open the financial picture — monthly surplus and savings. On learning there was neither, he did not run the rest of the open-wallet sequence (credit cards, available credit, investments) and instead introduced two lower price points not in the published offer: a 3-month tier at $4,000 (~$430/mo) and 12-month financing at '$650', then a $199/mo Primal University membership.

objections.raw_quote: I'm not in this stage in my life where I can just throw 10, 6, 10, 6 at something
objections.rep_response: Paused the call to message his next caller, then asked whether the prospect was open to an honest conversation about his finances.

objections.raw_quote: I think that like the best thing I could do now would just be, like I have to like crunch numbers on my end, it's not something I can do in real time.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it, offered a further downsell (Primal University), exchanged phone numbers and closed the call with 'anything, any other questions for me before we hop off?'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep: 'we do have like a like a financing option where people could split the payments over six months or sorry 12 months which does bring it down to that like six six fifty' — i.e. roughly $650/month over 12 months, a total that reconciles with neither the $6,000 nor the $9,000 tier. Separately quoted the invented 3-month tier as 'the total is 4k for that ... that one is like 4.30 per month that it breaks down to'.

evidence: Prospect: 'I'm thinking that I'm going to do some numbers on my end and get back to you.'
Prospect: 'I think that most likely I would, I'm going to try to make it work. I'm going to try, but ... it seems a little unrealistic at this point.'
Counter-evidence toward lost: he disclosed zero monthly surplus, zero savings, is not paying himself and cannot cover his own mortgage — 'I don't make any money whatsoever'
Counter-evidence toward lost: he named the low-tier Primal University as his likely starting point, not the 1:1 programme
No payment taken, no payment link sent, no next call booked — only phone numbers exchanged
outcome.next_step: Prospect to run his own numbers and text or email the rep; rep sent a text so the prospect has his number. Nothing scheduled.

notable.note: A prospect with genuinely zero discretionary cash was taken all the way through a full presentation and then offered four price points below the published offer in the space of about six minutes — $6,000/6mo down to $4,000/3mo, down to $650/mo financing, down to $199/mo. The screening that would have caught this (income, surplus, savings) happened after the price drop rather than before the presentation. Separately, the prospect is eating 1,200-1,280 kcal/day unsupervised and the rep proposed layering intermittent fasting on top without any question about medical oversight.

quality.notes: Repeated short-turn inversions. At 00:03:16 a line about the prospect's own work schedule is attributed to the rep; at 00:10:38 the rep's question 'Have you been dropping that?' is attributed to the prospect; at 00:47:48 the prospect's question 'it's like a thousand a month for six months?' is attributed to the rep; at 00:56:43 the price recital and the prospect's reply are inverted. Content-level facts are reliable, line-level attribution is not.
